newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary share prices bottom out, market firms.
newsitem.headline: Hungary share prices bottom out, market firms.

text.p: Hungarian share prices ended higher on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday as shares rebounded after seven days of decline, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 3,592.55 points, up 75.16.
BUX index futures closed higher for all maturities, by 10.00 to 70.50 points.
Traders saw several reasons behind the market turnaround, such as the positive impact of foreign markets, the end of profit-taking and expectations of good third-quarter results.
"The period of profit-taking is over," said Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB Rt.

"The bearish trend has lasted for quite a while, so the corrective phase might have reached a level (to trigger purchases)," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, adding that other bourses also changed direction.
"This can be attributed primarily to the U.S. market," she said.
Traders also said that investors were looking forward to the release of third quarter corporate results which have to be submitted to the bourse by November 15.
The biggest gainers were in the energy, pharmaceuticals and hotel sectors, with oil and gas company MOL one of the main beneficiaries, firming almost five percent or 75 forints to close at 1,620.
